what_happened: On a multi-lane highway, the recorded human driver moved one lane left. The policy instead kept straight in its own lane and sped up from about 4.5 to 6.7 m/s. Meanwhile actor 56, which had been just behind and to the left of the ego, moved ahead and edged into the ego's lane. At 7.2 s the ego's front-left clipped 56's rear corner, with the gap to 56 at 3.5 m. A trailing actor also struck the ego's rear.

On a busy multi-lane highway, the ego sped up from 4.2 to 6.8 m/s and kept to its own lane. Actor 56, which had been travelling beside it on the left, moved over in front of the ego: the gap to the car ahead fell from 21.8 m to 3.6 m within 0.5 s, and the ego's front clipped 56. The ego was 1.6 m from where the recorded car drove (that car moved left), so the replayed actor merged into a lane the ego still occupied. The ego was speeding up rather than holding back for the car beside it, but it had too little time to avoid the merge.

The ego was speeding up from 4.5 to 6.7 m/s on a multi-lane road and yawed left (on the map the lanes tilt against its heading), so its front-left hit actor 56, which was travelling next to it in the left adjacent lane. A following vehicle also hit the ego's rear, but the front contact with 56 happened first.

At about 4 m/s on a multi-lane highway, the ego drifted about 2 m left of its route and the recorded path, even though the command was RIGHT and then STRAIGHT. Actor 29, which was coming up from behind on the left, then sideswiped the ego's left side at 12.1 s. The front gap was over 27 m until the contact, so this was not a lead-vehicle collision.

On a straight multi-lane highway in slow traffic, the ego sped up from about 4 to 6.4 m/s and drifted about 1.6 m left of the recorded path (the ghost box), so its body crossed toward the lane boundary. It sideswiped actor 56, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane, and the collision was scored as lateral. The lead car stayed about 18 m or more ahead the whole time, so this was not a failure to brake for a lead vehicle.

On a multi-lane highway the ego slowed for no clear reason (5.3 to 3.3 m/s, lead 22+ m ahead) and drifted about 1.9 m left of the recorded path, partly into the next lane, where small actor 29, overtaking from behind, sideswiped its left-rear side.

After handoff the ego sped up from 4.5 to 6.7 m/s and drifted left toward the adjacent lane, roughly following the leftward recorded path. Its front hit the rear-right of actor 56, which was just ahead in that left lane. The rear contact from a following actor came after this front collision.

In slow, dense highway traffic going STRAIGHT, the ego was already closing on lead car 12 in its lane when the policy took over at 4.7 s (gap 5.5 m, closing at about 1.4 m/s). The policy slowed only a little (4.2 to 3.4 m/s) and planned a late swerve left, and its front clipped car 12 at 5.7 s. The ego was only about 0.2 to 0.6 m from where the human drove, so the takeover state was already very tight, and the collision may partly come from the replay or the box sizes.

On a congested multi-lane highway, the ego was following actor 13 at about 4.5 m/s when the policy's planned path (orange) swung left, away from the straight route. The ego drifted into the left adjacent lane and its front struck actor 61, which was travelling alongside slightly ahead in that lane.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego was slowing (4.9→3.5 m/s) and its plan wandered left of the recorded route, until it was about 2.2 m left of where the human drove and straddling the line into the left lane. A small actor (id 29, probably a motorcycle) coming up from behind in that lane hit the ego's left side.
